title: Super Metroid

masks.why: the energy, missiles and map display are BG3 laid out for 256 columns on a 32-tile map that would repeat

issues: The room layer (BG1) is drawn, with the level in work RAM: the game keeps the whole room in work RAM as 16 x 16 blocks ($7F:0002, its width and height at $7E:07A5 and $07A7, the block table at $7E:A000), so the sides show the room ahead before the game draws it, checked against the game's own picture every frame (shown only while the room in RAM is what the SNES picture shows). Beyond the room's edges the sides show the room's background (BG2) or the backdrop.

Side truth (Workshop --wms-side-truth, palette entries compared, 2026-10-25, 6,300 frames of the attract demos): BG1 99.4% right, 0% empty, 0.6% wrong (one moment: a place that changed between the side showing it and the SNES picture showing it 300 frames later). Before the level: 10.7% right, 88.7% empty; every layer extended, 88% wrong. BG2 extended: 100% right, 0% wrong (by colour it was 3.7% wrong: one room's spores fade their palette, CGRAM 113-115, between the side showing a place and the SNES picture showing it; the side shows the same tiles in the live palette, as the centre does).
The room's level is verified on 2,807 of the 2,808 frames that drew it; on a frame where it is not (a room loading) the sides fall back to what the game has drawn.
The status display's sides are left empty (BG3 filled in rows 0-31).
No flicker: in the 6,300 frames checked the game never drew more sprites on a line than a SNES shows, so it changed nothing; it changes only lines over the limits.
Fast CPU ran the 6,300 frames checked; the attract demos play differently (the game's timing changes from frame 10).

verified.how: Workshop --wms-test (E6), 6,300 frames of the attract demos in lockstep with the SNES console: widescreen's centre 256 columns identical to the SNES picture every frame (the level in work RAM on), STAT77 and the sound identical, switched off frame-identical; no flicker changes only lines over the SNES's limits; better sound changes only the sound; E8 side truth.
